title: Rear Suspension Diagnosis
introduction:
The rear suspension divides the work: springs support load, shocks control movement, and arms and links guide the wheels. The stabilizer bar couples the sides to resist body roll. I think of these as separate members of the same crew; handing every complaint to the shock absorber gives it a job description it can't possibly fulfill.

This page directs you to the required suspension diagnostic procedure. Its preparation, checks, result interpretation and decision branches are unavailable here, so this referral cannot serve as a standalone diagnostic walkthrough.

edits.text: For rear-suspension diagnosis, refer to [Suspension System](#/document/G1686610) (204-00 Suspension System - General Information, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The required reference supplies the diagnostic route for distinguishing complaints involving load support, motion control or wheel location. Knowing those component roles helps frame the complaint, but does not establish which part has failed.
